title: Xinbeitou Hot Springs Walk: MRT to Thermal Valley
excerpt: A 2 to 3 hour walk from Xinbeitou MRT through Beitou Park, past the Hot Spring Museum and the green library, to the steaming lake at Thermal Valley, with where to soak afterwards.
content:
Xinbeitou packs its best sights into one short, gently uphill valley, so this is the easiest of the self-guided walks on the site. You leave the MRT, follow the steaming Beitou River through the park, look round a Japanese-era bathhouse and a timber library, and finish at the sulphur lake that feeds much of the town's water. The numbered route is about 1.4km one way, or roughly 2.5km once you add the walk back down to the station, and with time inside each stop it takes 2 to 3 hours.

Two closures change the plan this season. The Beitou Hot Spring Museum shuts for restoration from 9 November 2026 until about late October 2027, so after that date you can only see it from outside. The Millennium Hot Spring open-air pool, beside the route, has been closed for rebuilding since January 2025. Several stops also close on Mondays, so check the best time to go before setting off. For more on the area itself, see the Xinbeitou guide.

The Route

Staying overnight makes the soak at the end far more relaxed; the Beitou hot spring hotels guide lists fourteen options by budget, with the distance of each from the station.

Step-By-Step

  • 1 Start at Xinbeitou MRT, the end of the short branch line from Beitou station
  • Leave the station and cross towards the green slope opposite, where Zhongshan Road and Guangming Road split either side of the park
  • The smell of sulphur usually reaches you before the park does, which is a good sign you are heading the right way
  • 2 Walk into Beitou Park at its lower, western end
    • The park covers about six hectares along the Beitou River, and the water running through it is warm enough to steam on cool days
    • Look for the lily pond and its wooden pavilion, then follow the stream uphill past the series of small waterfalls
    • [optional] The Ketagalan Culture Center stands just across Zhongshan Road, with exhibitions on Taiwan's Pingpu indigenous peoples, including the Ketagalan of northern Taiwan. It opens Tuesday to Sunday, 09:00–17:00, and is closed on Mondays
  • 3 Carry on up the Zhongshan Road side of the park to the Beitou Hot Spring Museum
    • Opened in 1913 as the town’s public bathhouse, the brick and half-timbered building now explains how the springs work and how the town grew around them. There is no bathing here
    • Entry is free. Opening hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–18:00, with last entry at 17:45, and it is closed on Mondays
    • Shoes come off at the door in exchange for slippers, and no more than 200 visitors are allowed in at once, so expect a short queue at busy times
    • Free guided tours in Mandarin run Tuesday to Friday at 11:00, 14:00 and 16:00, lasting about 30 minutes. There are none at weekends
    • Closed from 9 November 2026 to about late October 2027 for restoration work. During that time the exterior can still be seen from the park
  • 4 Cross the park to the Guangming Road side and the Beitou Library
    • This branch of the Taipei Public Library was the first building in Taiwan to be certified as a green building. It is mostly wood and steel, with solar panels on the roof and rainwater collected for the toilets and plants
    • Visitors are welcome to look round. It is a working library, so keep voices low and photos discreet
    • Opening hours are Tuesday to Saturday 08:30–21:00, and Sunday and Monday 09:00–17:00. It closes on the first Thursday of each month (5 November and 3 December 2026) and on national holidays, including Election Day on 28 November 2026
  • Leave the library and head uphill along Guangming Road. You pass Longnaitang, the old bathhouse covered in Add a Soak, and then the fenced-off site of the Millennium Hot Spring, closed for rebuilding
  • [optional] Cross to the Plum Garden on Zhongshan Road, a late-1930s Japanese house that was the summer home of the calligrapher Yu You-ren. It is open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00–18:00, and closed on Mondays
  • [optional] Higher up on Wenquan Road, Puji Temple is a small temple set back among the trees, listed by Taipei Travel as open daily from 09:00 to 17:00
  • 5 Follow Zhongshan Road to its upper end and the entrance to Thermal Valley
    • A milky green lake fills the valley floor, with steam hanging over it all year. It is one of the sources that supplies Beitou's hot spring water
    • The water here is between 80 and 100°C, so the paths are fenced and bathing is impossible. Boiling eggs in it, once a local habit, is now banned
    • The spring is the acidic “green sulphur” type, and the valley gives its name to hokutolite (Beitou stone), a mildly radioactive mineral found only here and at Tamagawa in Japan
    • Entry is free. Hours are 09:00–17:00 every day except Monday

From Thermal Valley it is downhill all the way back to Xinbeitou MRT, roughly 15 minutes on foot.

Add a Soak

The Millennium Hot Spring, the swimsuit-only open-air pool in the park, closed on 24 January 2025 for rebuilding. The works were scheduled to finish during 2026, but as of 27 October 2026 no reopening date had been published, so do not plan around it. These are the options that are open:

  • Longnaitang on Guangming Road: an old indoor bathhouse with separate men's and women's baths, bathed nude. NT$150 per session; sessions run 06:30–11:00, 12:00–17:00 and 18:00–21:00, and it is closed on Wednesdays. Ages 6 and up, with under-12s accompanied by an adult. Towels are not included (NT$50 to buy one). Private family rooms start at NT$400 an hour for two
  • A foot bath: Longnaitang's garden foot bath costs NT$100 for 40 minutes with a drink, Thursday to Sunday 14:00–19:00. It closes for the summer, roughly June to September
  • Hotel public baths and private rooms: many Beitou hotels sell day entry to their baths without an overnight stay. As examples, Beitou Hot Spring Resort (Tian Yue Quan) charges NT$700 on weekdays for its nude public bath in the winter season, Radium Kagaya NT$1,200 plus 10% on weekdays, and Spring City NT$800 for its outdoor swimsuit-and-cap pools. Private rooms at Kagaya start at NT$2,000 plus 10% for 90 minutes. The Beitou hot spring hotels guide has the full list with age limits and booking rules

A few rules apply almost everywhere. Shower properly before getting in, keep your towel out of the water, and tie long hair up. Gender-separated baths are nude, while mixed pools need a swimsuit (and often a cap). Phones are not allowed in nude baths, and bathhouses ask you not to soak after drinking alcohol or on a completely empty or very full stomach. The Taipei hot springs guide covers etiquette in more detail.

Where to Eat

The route itself has little food once you are inside the park, so eat near the station first or after you finish. Zhongshan Road and Guangming Road both have small restaurants and convenience stores close to Xinbeitou MRT. For something more traditional, Beitou Market on Guangming Road, down towards Beitou station, is known for local snacks. Longnaitang's garden foot bath also serves snacks and afternoon tea on the days it opens.

For a sit-down meal, several of the hotels have restaurants open to non-guests; the hotels guide lists which ones. Combining lunch with a private bath is a common way to spend an afternoon here.

Best Time to Go

  • Tuesday to Friday is best. Every stop is open, the museum runs its free tours, and the paths are quieter than at weekends
  • Avoid Mondays. The museum, Thermal Valley, the Plum Garden and the Ketagalan Culture Center are all closed, leaving only the park and the library
  • Start by early afternoon, because Thermal Valley closes at 17:00
  • If you want to bathe at Longnaitang, avoid Wednesdays
  • To see the museum inside, go before it closes on 9 November 2026. After that, the walk still works for the park, library and Thermal Valley
  • November to March is hot spring season, when the cooler air makes a soak more pleasant and the steam over the valley more visible

Getting There and Back

Start: Xinbeitou MRT. Take the red Tamsui-Xinyi line to Beitou, then change to the one-stop branch line to Xinbeitou. From Taipei Main Station, the fare is NT$35 on an EasyCard, and the journey takes about half an hour including the change.

Finish: Thermal Valley. Walk back down to Xinbeitou MRT in about 15 minutes, or catch minibus S25 (小25), which links Thermal Valley with Xinbeitou and Beitou MRT stations.

To carry on to Yangmingshan National Park, go back to Beitou MRT and take minibus S9 or bus 230. Alternatively, ride the red line north to Tamsui for the riverside at sunset.

Common Questions

Is the Beitou Hot Spring Museum open?

It is open Tuesday to Sunday until 8 November 2026. From 9 November 2026 it is closed for restoration, with reopening planned for late October 2027. The exact date will be announced by the museum.

Has the Millennium Hot Spring reopened?

Not as of 27 October 2026. It has been closed for rebuilding since 24 January 2025, and no reopening date had been announced. Longnaitang and the hotel baths are the alternatives nearby.

Can you get in the water at Thermal Valley?

No. The lake is between 80 and 100°C and fenced off. It is for looking only, and it costs nothing to visit.

How long is the Xinbeitou walk?

About 1.4km from the station to Thermal Valley, or roughly 2.5km with the walk back. Allow 2 to 3 hours with time inside the stops, plus extra if you add a soak.

Which day should I avoid?

Monday, when the museum, Thermal Valley, the Plum Garden and the Ketagalan Culture Center are all closed. Tuesday to Friday is the quietest time when everything is open.
